rows.uncertainty: Unit: the 80.65% is a mean over 1938 graft sheets, not over patients or lesions; [sheets per lesion and per patient are not in abstract]. Whether the mean is over sheets or a mean of per-patient means is not in abstract. Percentage repigmentation is not colour match. Diagnosis: [not an IGH study]; vitiligo vulgaris and segmental vitiligo, a Module 5-damage-repair lead (cell transplantation with the longest colour-match follow-up named in the transplant search, PR 41) entered at Gate A; it says nothing directly about IGH spots. [Module 5-damage-repair is not an allowed module in tools/ledger.py, so the row is filed under 1-hypopigmentation with an ADJACENT diagnosis, as mulekar2007, lin2024 and elhoshy2025 are.] Abstract only. Design (retrospective or prospective, recall or examination), how and by whom repigmentation and colour match were graded, the cut-offs for excellent, good, fair and poor, and whether photographs or an instrument were used are all not in abstract. Follow-up 'up to 13 years after treatment (mean 1.87 years)' is per cohort; the time at which each patient was graded is not in abstract, and the abstract does not say whether 'treatment' means the final treatment or whether phototherapy or repeat grafting followed, so months after the final treatment are NOT_DERIVABLE. A mean of 1.87 years with a maximum of 13 means [many patients were graded well under 2 years after treatment]. Internal contradiction in the vitiligo vulgaris results: the counts 110, 18, 4 and 12 sum to [144], not 173, while the percentages 63.6, 10.4, 5.8 and 20.2 sum to [100.0]; 110 and 18 fit 173 ([63.6%] and [10.4%]), but 4 of 173 is [2.3%], not 5.8%, and 12 of 173 is [6.9%], not 20.2%. 5.8% and 20.2% of 173 would be about [10] and [35] patients, which would sum to [173]; [the fair and poor counts look copied from the segmental line]. Which numbers are right needs the full text. The segmental counts 83, 10, 4 and 12 sum to [109] and fit their percentages. The abstract mentions '45 no repigmentation patients', which matches neither the poor counts as printed ([12 + 12 = 24]) nor as implied by the percentages ([about 35 + 12 = 47]); whether 'no repigmentation' is the same as 'poor' is not in abstract. Koebner phenomenon at the donor site and new lesions elsewhere were more frequent in those 45 patients (no numbers in abstract); [donor-site depigmentation is a harm of the method, not a colour-match result]. The Background says the technique 'is available for the treatment of stable vitiligo' as general background; [whether all treated patients had stable disease, and for how long, is not in abstract], although the Conclusions name 'the stability time before transplantation' as a factor.

quotes.quote: We investigated the long-term percentage of repigmentation and colour matching up to 13 years after treatment (mean 1.87 years).

We performed a follow-up study involving 173 patients (95 male, 78 female) with vitiligo vulgaris and 109 patients (59 male, 50 female) with segmental vitiligo who underwent autologous epidermal grafting.
In patients with vitiligo vulgaris, 110 (63.6%) showed excellent repigmentation, 18 (10.4%) showed good, 4 (5.8%) showed fair and 12 (20.2%) showed poor repigmentation.
In patients with segmental vitiligo, 83 (76%) showed excellent repigmentation, 10 (9%) showed good, 4 (4%) showed fair and 12 (11%) showed poor repigmentation.
There was a higher ratio of Koebner phenomenon on the donor site and new lesions on the other sites in 45 no repigmentation patients.
We investigated the long-term percentage of repigmentation and colour matching up to 13 years after treatment (mean 1.87 years).
Autologous epidermal transplantation is available for the treatment of stable vitiligo.
